subject: Re: Evidence & runbook request: tenant segmentation, VPC peering, and residency controls
messages:
From: Anna Morales <security@healthgrid.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Evidence request: tenant segmentation + private peering for upcoming audit

Hi Ben,

We're kicking off our vendor audit window and need documentation demonstrating how Redwood confines HealthGrid workloads to EU-only compute and networks when we use the Private deployment option. Specifically we need:

- A concise runbook describing tenant segmentation and routing (how instances are placed into EU-only pools and how traffic is prevented from leaving the region).
- Network diagram for the VPC peering/privatelink setup (showing subnets, endpoints, and any proxy/bastion components).
- A short matrix mapping SIG/CAIQ controls to artifacts you can provide (token retention, KV cache boundaries, KMS key partitioning).
- Any logs or attestations we can use for our SOC 2 vendor evidence pack (rotation events, ephemeral key audit entries or HSM/KMS identifiers).

Can we get a draft by end of day Wednesday (2027-06-23)? Also, please confirm whether there are third-party endpoints (cloud-region CDNs, monitoring agents) that may egress outside EU during failover scenarios.

Thanks,
Anna Morales
Security Manager, HealthGrid


From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Morales <security@healthgrid.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-20T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: tenant segmentation + private peering for upcoming audit

Anna — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. Quick plan and owner assignment:

- Runbook + diagram (deliverable: PDF + SVG): owner — irene_choi. She'll include operational steps for provisioning EU-only pools, tenant mapping, and automated checks that gate deployment.
- SIG/CAIQ mapping spreadsheet: owner — me (ben_carter) with inputs from Karthik for cryptography/KMS boundaries.
- Auditables (rotation logs / ephemeral key events): owner — karthik_iyer. He will pull KMS rotation entries and anonymized request IDs that align to HealthGrid tenant IDs.

Two clarifications from our side:
1) For failover we have a configured standby peering option that remains disabled by default for customers who opt-in to strict residency. If you have strict EU-only required, we will mark your account with "geo-lock: strict" which disables global fallback and will require manual approval to change.
2) Monitoring metrics (prometheus push gateway / alert ingesters) use a centralized telemetry aggregator that is deployed in-region for strict-residency accounts. Exporters to third-party SaaS (if enabled by you) may be configured to use EU endpoints only; we'll note the configuration keys in the runbook.

Timeline: aiming to share all artifacts in draft form by 2027-06-22 EOD; finalized package by 2027-06-24. If that works, I'll kick off the deliverables. Also proposing a quick 30-min call tomorrow to walk the runbook and call out any gaps — can you do 2027-06-21 11:00 CET?

Ben
Director, Product Security (on behalf of Ops)
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Anna Morales <security@healthgrid.com>
Date: 2027-06-21T08:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: tenant segmentation + private peering for upcoming audit

Ben / team — attaching a first draft runbook and a cropped network diagram (see attachments). Highlights included in the doc:

- Tenant allocation flow: how account metadata maps to placement constraints (eu-only tag), gating checks in the admission controller, and automated policy enforcement.
- Operational play: steps for performing a manual verification (on-call checklist) and a sample audit command to enumerate active tenant placements.
- Failover controls: explicit instructions that standby peering is set to "manual enable" for "geo-lock: strict" customers and who to contact to request an exception.

Notes / asks for Anna: can you confirm whether HealthGrid requires the KMS key material to be customer-managed (bring-your-own-key)? If so, Karthik will include the BYOK mapping and a short list of HSM identifiers we can provide for your audit.

Irene
Sr. Technical Program Manager, Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Morales <security@healthgrid.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-22T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Final: residency evidence & next steps

Anna — attaching the draft package per your request: runbook (redwood-tenant-isolation-runbook-v1.2.pdf), residency matrix (sig-lite-residency-matrix.xlsx), and a high-res network segmentation diagram (network-segmentation-diagram.png).

What we've included:
- Runbook with operator run-through and an "audit mode" checklist that extracts the last 90 days of placement and peering events tied to HealthGrid tenant IDs.
- Residency matrix mapping SIG categories to artifacts (example: "Data Location" -> region-bound placement logs; "Key Management" -> KMS key IDs and rotation timestamps).
- Diagram showing VPC peering, privatelink endpoints, and the collector agents that remain in-region.

Next steps: can we schedule the 30-min review call to walk the runbook? Proposed slots (CET): 2027-06-22 14:00, 2027-06-23 09:30. Also confirming that our "geo-lock: strict" flag will be applied to HealthGrid accounts upon signature of the residency addendum — I'll route the addendum and a DocuSign link after you confirm preferred slot.

Let us know if anything else is required for your SOC 2 packet.

Thanks,
Ben
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
